prompt:
Write 7 short claim log entries (one to three sentences each) by an auto insurance adjuster for a rear-end collision claim, in time order. Injury: whiplash. The claimant is represented by a lawyer. Start each entry on a new line with 'Entry 1:', 'Entry 2:' and so on. No names, dates or amounts. (Internal reference C-1418; do not mention it.) Work these facts into the text naturally, in your own words, without listing them:
- It is not yet clear whether the injury came from this crash.
- Treatment ran somewhat longer than usual for this injury.
- No earlier injury to the same body area is known.
- Photos confirm some details, but there are no independent witnesses.
- The damage is mostly in line with the described impact.
- The claimant told the same account in every conversation.
- The police and witnesses confirm the claimant was in the vehicle.
- A few old scratches may be older than this crash.
- A neighbor thinks the car was damaged some weeks before the claimed date.
- The driver is named on the policy.
text:
Entry 1: First notice of loss received for a rear-end collision in which the insured's vehicle was struck from behind while stopped at a traffic signal. The claimant is represented by counsel, and all further contact is being routed through the attorney's office.

Entry 2: Confirmed the driver is named on the policy and the policy was in force at the time of loss. Police report reflects the claimant was present in the vehicle, and the responding officer's notes match the parties' statements on the general sequence of events.

Entry 3: Reviewed scene and vehicle photographs. Damage to the rear of the claimant's vehicle is largely consistent with the described impact, though a few old scratches on the bumper area may predate this crash and will need to be separated out during appraisal.

Entry 4: Spoke with a neighbor who reported seeing the vehicle with rear damage several weeks before the claimed date of loss. The statement is unverified and has been noted for follow-up, since no independent witness has come forward for this collision.

Entry 5: Claimant's account has remained the same across every conversation, including the initial call and the recorded statement given through counsel. Medical records show whiplash diagnosis, with no prior injury to the neck or upper back found in the history provided so far.

Entry 6: Treatment has continued somewhat longer than is typical for this type of soft-tissue injury. It is not yet clear whether all of the treatment is related to this crash, and a records review has been requested to address causation.

Entry 7: File remains open pending receipt of complete medical records, the appraisal with the scratch allocation, and the outcome of the neighbor follow-up. Next review is scheduled once counsel responds to the records request.
